newsitem.title: UK: TI Group expects further growth.
newsitem.headline: TI Group expects further growth.

text.p: International engineering firm TI Group Plc reported an eight percent rise in half-year profits on Thursday and said it expected further growth although sterling's strength would continue to weigh on translation of foreign sales and profits.

Underlying pre-tax profits rose to 112.1 million pounds ($183.1 million), from 103.7 million pounds before exceptional gains of 21.6 million pounds last year, on sales up four percent at 932.6 million pounds.

The company said organic sales growth was nine percent after adjusting for acquisitions and disposals and the impact of exchange rates. The strength of the pound mainly hit translation of overseas results, reducing reported group sales by 70 million pounds and group pretax profit by 7.6 million pounds.

"We go forward with strong order books, are well positioned to make further bolt-on acquisitions and have confidence in our ability to generate continued growth," chairman Sir Christopher Lewinton said.
"Our global spread and balance saw the group achieve a strong first-half result with organic profit growth of 15 percent, improved margins and good cashflow.
"Our currency exposure is limited in the main to translation, not transaction, as we manufacture in some 45 countries around the world. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
